answer: A credible mechanism is a rate-limited bridge from identity to economic influence: each agent must lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can post offers or vote, and its weight grows only with verified, completed exchanges over time. New identities therefore cannot instantly multiply influence; they must fund separate deposits and wait through a reputation horizon. If they misbehave, the stake is forfeited, so an attacker pays real capital for every sybil, while honest agents earn nectar from useful trades.
